Order means the most recent paid, unshipped order. An address can change until the carrier label is printed.

Order #48213: paid, not yet labelled, warehouse Leipzig. Lineage recorded against the answer.

Gather line 2’s schedule, open orders, component availability and changeover matrix.
Query the MES and the ERP — line 2 and its open orders only.
Order 4471 blocked until Thursday; orders 4468 and 4473 have penalties; changeover matrix loaded. Lineage recorded.
What do we already know about line 2?
Kessler slipped twice this quarter. Procedure: ask the supplier’s agent for a firm date before committing.
Context assembled inside 2,100 tokens: schedule, orders, availability, changeovers, supplier history.
Time to reason. The call goes through the gateway rather than straight to a provider.

Had the delay fit inside the existing buffer, this branch would have re-sequenced unattended.
Execute publish_schedule with an idempotency key, so a retry cannot publish twice.

messages.label: task arrives on a channel
messages.carries: The task itself, plus the identity and entitlements of whoever is asking.
messages.story: Maya messages support: “Can you ship my order to my office instead?” She has already paid.
messages.contract: Authenticated channel session or API credential.
watch: Under-specified intent with no path to ask a clarifying question
Service-account identity that erases whose entitlements apply
messages.how: Channel adapter normalises text, voice or image into one request envelope; stream from the first token.
messages.wire: Channel-native: WebSocket or SSE for chat, WebRTC for voice, HTTPS REST or a signed webhook for API callers. TLS 1.3, OIDC-authenticated session.

messages.label: session and tenant context
messages.carries: The normalised request with session and tenant context attached.
messages.story: The chat surface opens a session, attaches Maya’s account and her company’s tenant, and passes the request on.
messages.contract: Internal request envelope: tenant, session, channel, modality.
watch: Tenant inferred from the session rather than asserted explicitly
messages.how: Session store keyed by tenant; tenant and user come from verified token claims, never from the message body.
messages.wire: Internal HTTPS/JSON over the service mesh (mTLS); session read from Redis over RESP.

messages.label: screen before spending a token
messages.carries: The request, on its way to be screened before anything is spent.
messages.story: Before a single token is spent, the gateway asks the guardrails to look at the message.
messages.contract: Synchronous guardrail call at the gateway edge, fail-closed.
watch: Fail-open behaviour when the guardrail service is slow or unavailable
Screening treated as sufficient because it happened at the edge
messages.how: Gateway pre-request hook calls the guardrail service synchronously, fail-closed, inside a latency budget.
stack: LiteLLM or Envoy AI Gateway hooks
messages.wire: Synchronous gRPC (mTLS) from the gateway’s pre-request hook to the guardrail service, with a deadline inside the latency budget; REST fallback.

messages.label: cleared · scoped agent identity
messages.carries: Clearance, plus a short-lived credential scoped to this task for the agent that will act.
messages.story: Nothing hostile, no card numbers. The agent that will act receives a credential scoped to Maya’s account and valid for minutes, not months.
messages.contract: Just-in-time credential bound to this task and this trace ID.
watch: Long-lived credentials issued because short-lived ones were inconvenient
Scope granted for the whole session rather than the specific action
messages.how: Workload identity for the agent, exchanged for a short-lived token scoped to this task and trace.
messages.wire: gRPC response; workload identity from the SPIFFE Workload API over a Unix domain socket; task-scoped token via OAuth 2.1 token exchange over HTTPS.

messages.label: plan, inside this budget
messages.carries: The cleared task and the budget ceiling it must complete within.
messages.story: The gateway hands the task to the orchestrator with a ceiling: forty steps and a few cents of budget.
messages.contract: Budget envelope plus step and termination limits, attached to the trace.
watch: A budget checked only at ingress, so an expensive loop is discovered too late
messages.how: Budget and step ceilings travel in the trace context; the workflow is started with hard limits.
stack: Temporal workflow with max-step and timeout
messages.wire: gRPC to the durable-execution server (Temporal StartWorkflow) or HTTPS POST to the orchestrator; budget travels as W3C baggage.

messages.label: what do these terms mean?
messages.carries: The planned sub-task, in whatever words the user and planner used.
messages.story: What does “my order” mean here — which order, and what does “shipped” mean in this business?
messages.contract: Task description plus the entities and metrics it mentions.
watch: Skipping grounding entirely and retrieving on raw user phrasing
messages.how: Entity linking against the glossary and a semantic-layer lookup for every metric the task names.
stack: dbt semantic layer / MetricFlow or Cube API
messages.wire: GraphQL or REST to the semantic layer (Cube REST/GraphQL; dbt Semantic Layer GraphQL or JDBC/Arrow Flight SQL); mTLS.

messages.label: resolved entities and metrics
messages.carries: The same request, now unambiguous: resolved entities, agreed metric definitions, applicable rules.
messages.story: Order means the most recent paid, unshipped order. An address can change until the carrier label is printed.
messages.contract: Defined query — the terms mean what the warehouse thinks they mean.
watch: Definitions resolved but not carried through, so retrieval falls back to keywords
messages.how: Canonical identifiers and metric definitions returned as structured context, not prose.
messages.wire: GraphQL/REST response (JSON-LD or plain JSON) on the same connection.

messages.label: assemble context for this step
messages.carries: A request for the evidence this reasoning step needs, with a token budget attached.
messages.story: Gather what this step needs: the order, its fulfilment status and the office address.
messages.contract: Context request bounded by budget and by the acting identity.
watch: No budget passed, so retrieval optimises for recall and the context window pays for it
messages.how: Retrieval request carries an explicit token budget; tool definitions are retrieved, not preloaded.
messages.wire: In-process call when retrieval is a library; gRPC (mTLS) when it is a separate service. Token budget as a request field.

messages.label: governed rows and columns
messages.carries: A query against systems of record, evaluated for the identity the agent acts under.
messages.story: Query the order system — but only the rows Maya is entitled to see.
messages.contract: Data contract plus row and column policy for the acting identity.
watch: Entitlements applied at query time but lost once results enter the context window
messages.how: Federated query with row and column policy evaluated for the acting identity, exposed as an MCP data server.
stack: Apache Ranger or OPA row-column policy
messages.wire: MCP over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0) to the data server; underneath, the engine’s own protocol — Trino HTTP client protocol / JDBC, Arrow Flight SQL, or the warehouse driver.

messages.label: data with lineage and entitlements
messages.carries: Governed rows and columns, with lineage events emitted and freshness guaranteed by contract.
messages.story: Order #48213: paid, not yet labelled, warehouse Leipzig. Lineage recorded against the answer.
messages.contract: Data plus provenance; anything stale or out of contract is refused rather than returned quietly.
watch: Stale sources answering confidently because freshness is not enforced
Lineage dropped, so an incorrect answer cannot be traced
messages.how: Data contract checked on the way out; lineage event emitted for the rows returned.
messages.wire: JSON-RPC result over the same MCP session; lineage emitted separately as OpenLineage events over HTTP (or Kafka).

messages.label: what do we already know?
messages.carries: A recall request scoped to this tenant and this user.
messages.story: Do we already know anything about Maya?
messages.contract: Tenant-partitioned lookup; no cross-tenant reads under any circumstances.
watch: Shared stores with a careless key allowing cross-tenant recall
messages.how: Tenant-partitioned recall over vector and key-value stores with a relevance and recency score.
stack: Qdrant or pgvector namespace per tenant
messages.wire: gRPC to the vector store (Qdrant gRPC) or PostgreSQL wire protocol (pgvector); key-value recall over RESP; a memory service exposes REST.

messages.label: episodic, semantic, procedural
messages.carries: Prior episodes, learned facts and the procedures this organisation follows.
messages.story: She changed an address once before, to the same office. Procedure: validate the address against the postal service first.
messages.contract: Recall with provenance per fact, so a remembered claim can be checked.
watch: Recall that is confident and wrong, because nothing scores whether a memory is still true
Memory poisoning surviving indefinitely because nothing expires
messages.how: Memory records carry provenance, confidence and TTL; expired or low-confidence entries are filtered before return.
messages.wire: gRPC/REST response; provenance fields inline.

messages.label: context inside the token budget
messages.carries: The assembled context package: evidence, citations, tool definitions, inside the token budget.
messages.story: Context assembled inside 1,200 tokens: order, status, office address, and the rule about labels.
messages.contract: Token-budgeted context with citations preserved.
watch: Budget exceeded and silently truncated in the middle, where models attend least
Citations dropped during compaction, making the answer unverifiable
messages.how: Hybrid search, rerank, then prune and compact to the budget; citations preserved through compaction.
messages.wire: In-process or gRPC return to the orchestrator; context object serialised as JSON with citations.

messages.label: reason over this context
messages.carries: The reasoning request — sent through the gateway rather than direct to a provider.
messages.story: Time to reason. The call goes through the gateway rather than straight to a provider.
messages.contract: OpenAI-compatible call; no direct provider access from inside the loop.
watch: Direct calls that bypass the gateway, erasing quota, cost and policy at once
messages.how: OpenAI-compatible call through the gateway client with trace headers; direct provider access blocked at the network.
messages.wire: HTTPS REST, OpenAI-compatible JSON, to the gateway; SSE for streaming; W3C traceparent header; no direct provider egress (blocked at the mesh).

messages.label: routed, cached, metered
messages.carries: The call, routed to a model tier, served from cache where possible, and metered.
messages.story: Routed to the mid-tier model. The shared prefix is served from cache; tokens are metered to the retail tenant.
messages.contract: Routing decision plus a cost record keyed to the trace.
watch: Cache keys that omit tenant, leaking one tenant's answer to another
messages.how: Semantic routing rule picks the tier; prefix cache serves the shared prompt; cost record written per call.
messages.wire: HTTPS REST (OpenAI-compatible) from the gateway to the inference server; inside the cluster optionally gRPC via the KServe v2 / Triton inference protocol.

messages.label: inference on a pinned model
messages.carries: The prompt and context, to a version-pinned model.
messages.story: The model reads the context.
messages.contract: Pinned model version with a documented deprecation date.
watch: Unpinned versions changing behaviour silently between releases
messages.how: Serve a version-pinned model with continuous batching; the pin lives in the registry, not in code.
messages.wire: In-process engine call (vLLM, llm-d, SGLang); tensor-parallel shards talk over NCCL / RDMA, not an API.

messages.label: completion
messages.carries: The completion, with token counts.
messages.story: Completion: propose updating the shipping address on #48213 to the office address.
messages.contract: Structured output against the declared schema.
watch: Prose returned where a schema was expected, then parsed with a regular expression
messages.how: Constrained decoding against the declared schema so the completion is structurally valid by construction.
stack: vLLM guided decoding or provider structured outputs
messages.wire: In-process return; tokens streamed back through the serving layer.

messages.label: next action, schema-valid
messages.carries: A structured proposal for the next action — which tool, which arguments, with what confidence.
messages.story: A structured proposal, schema-valid: tool update_shipping_address, order 48213, the new address, confidence high.
messages.contract: Schema-valid structured output, validated before it is scored.
watch: Schema validity assumed rather than checked
Confidence taken from the model's own words rather than measured
messages.how: Validate the proposal at the boundary; confidence comes from validators and calibration, not the model's own words.
messages.wire: HTTPS REST response (JSON) or SSE stream; validated against JSON Schema at the boundary.

messages.label: score against autonomy policy
messages.carries: The proposed action, for scoring against the autonomy policy.
messages.story: Is this action allowed to run unattended?
messages.contract: Policy-as-code evaluated per action, not per session.
watch: The gate placed after execution, which makes it a log rather than a control
messages.how: Policy-as-code evaluated per action with impact, reversibility, data sensitivity, regulation and confidence as inputs.
messages.wire: REST POST to OPA (/v1/data) or an in-process Cedar / OPA-WASM evaluation; decision logged over HTTP to the decision-log sink.

messages.label: approval at a durable checkpoint
messages.carries: An approval request, with the action and the evidence behind it, paused at a durable checkpoint.
messages.cond: only if the action is irreversible, financial or regulated
messages.story: An address change on a paid order becomes irreversible the moment the label prints, so a human confirms. Jonas on the support desk sees the request with the evidence behind it.
messages.contract: The task waits without holding resources and resumes from the snapshot.
watch: A reviewer shown the action but not the evidence
Approval fatigue from too many low-stakes interruptions
messages.how: Durable interrupt: the workflow checkpoints, releases compute, and surfaces an approval task with the evidence pack.
stack: Temporal signal-and-wait or LangGraph interrupt + checkpointer
messages.wire: Durable interrupt persisted over gRPC (Temporal) or via the checkpointer’s database; approval task pushed to the surface over SSE/WebSocket (AG-UI events).

messages.label: human decision
messages.carries: The human decision, recorded against the trace with the approver identity.
messages.cond: only if the action is irreversible, financial or regulated
messages.story: Jonas approves in forty seconds. His decision is written to the trace.
messages.contract: Decision written to the audit trail before execution resumes.
watch: Resumption that replays side effects already executed before the pause
messages.how: The human decision is a signal that resumes the workflow from the snapshot; approver identity is written to the audit trail.
messages.wire: Human decision arrives over HTTPS POST from the surface and resumes the workflow as a Temporal Signal over gRPC; audit record appended over HTTPS.

messages.label: proceed unattended, logged
messages.carries: Permission to proceed unattended, because the action is reversible and low impact.
messages.story: Had the order been unpaid, this branch would have run unattended and fully logged instead.
messages.contract: Recorded policy decision carried on the trace.
watch: Approval granted for a class of actions rather than this action
messages.how: Autonomous path: the policy decision is recorded on the trace and the action proceeds under on-the-loop monitoring.
messages.wire: In-process or gRPC return from the policy evaluation; decision attribute on the span.

messages.label: execute the typed tool call
messages.carries: The typed tool call, with validated arguments and an idempotency key.
messages.story: Execute update_shipping_address, with an idempotency key so a retry cannot change the address twice.
messages.contract: Typed contract with declared inputs, outputs and error semantics.
watch: Arguments validated only in the model's output, not at the tool boundary
Write calls without idempotency keys, so a retry duplicates the effect
messages.how: Typed tool call executed as a workflow activity with an idempotency key and an explicit retry policy.
messages.wire: Temporal Activity dispatch (gRPC, task queue) or gRPC to the tool runner; idempotency key in metadata.

messages.label: provision an isolated sandbox
messages.carries: A request for isolation proportionate to the blast radius of this call.
messages.story: The tool runs in isolation — provision a sandbox proportionate to a write against an order system.
messages.contract: Default-deny egress, ephemeral filesystem, root dropped, no host secrets inside.
watch: Generated code executed with no sandbox at all because it was only a read
messages.how: Sandbox class chosen per tool blast radius, drawn from a warm pool.
messages.wire: Kubernetes API (HTTPS REST) for a pod with a RuntimeClass, or the Firecracker REST API over a Unix socket; E2B-style SDKs speak WebSocket.

messages.label: microVM, gVisor or Wasm ready
messages.carries: The sandbox: a microVM at roughly 125–150 ms, an application kernel, or a Wasm runtime under 5 ms.
messages.story: A microVM is ready in about 140 milliseconds, with no host secrets inside it.
messages.contract: Isolation chosen per tool class rather than once for the platform.
watch: Wasm chosen for its start time where the tool needs native libraries it cannot use
messages.how: Default-deny egress, ephemeral filesystem, dropped root, no host secrets mounted.
messages.wire: Runtime handle returned over the same channel; container runtime via CRI (gRPC) for gVisor; Wasmtime is an in-process host call.

messages.label: classify, rerank or forecast
messages.carries: A decision that a classifier, reranker, forecaster or optimiser will answer better.
messages.cond: only when a classical model answers it better
messages.story: Optional detour: the address-validation classifier is cheaper and more accurate than asking the model.
messages.contract: Tool contract like any other, with accuracy and drift monitoring attached.
watch: The LLM path used for a repeated decision a small model already answers better
messages.how: A classical model served behind the same tool contract as any other tool.
messages.wire: gRPC (KServe v2 inference protocol / BentoML / Seldon) or REST for small models; feature vector as protobuf or JSON.

messages.label: score or plan, far cheaper
messages.carries: A score, ranking or plan, at a fraction of the cost and latency of a language model.
messages.cond: only when a classical model answers it better
messages.story: Valid and deliverable, score 0.97, in four milliseconds.
messages.contract: Deterministic, versioned output with a monitored error rate.
watch: Drift unmonitored because these models sit outside agent telemetry
messages.how: Versioned scoring with drift monitored in the same telemetry as the agent.
messages.wire: gRPC/REST response with score and model version.

messages.label: cross on a standard contract
messages.carries: The call, handed to the protocol layer so the framework on either side stays replaceable.
messages.story: The call crosses the boundary on MCP, so the order system could be swapped without touching the agent.
messages.contract: Standard contract — MCP, A2A, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI — rather than bespoke glue.
watch: Bespoke integrations that make the framework expensive to change later
messages.how: MCP client with the server pinned by version and signature, scanned before first use, behind an MCP gateway.
messages.wire: MCP over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0) with OAuth 2.1 bearer tokens, through the MCP gateway; stdio only for local servers.

messages.label: MCP to systems · A2A to peers
messages.carries: The read or write, executed against the real system under the agent's scoped identity.
messages.story: Order management system: update the shipping address on #48213.
messages.contract: MCP request or A2A task; peer agents negotiate through agent cards and a task lifecycle.
watch: Third-party MCP servers unsigned, unscanned and unpinned
Insecure inter-agent communication once peers are involved (OWASP ASI07)
messages.how: An MCP server in front of the order system, or an A2A task to a peer agent with its own lifecycle.
messages.wire: The MCP server speaks the system’s native protocol (REST/OData, SOAP, JDBC, message bus); peer agents over A2A — JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTPS with gRPC and REST bindings, agent card at /.well-known.

messages.label: result or task handle
messages.carries: The result, an artifact, or a handle to a long-running task.
messages.story: Updated. A new carrier label is queued.
messages.contract: Typed response; long-running work returns a task handle rather than blocking.
watch: Peer agent output trusted as internal data rather than screened as external input
messages.how: Typed response; long-running work returns a task handle and completes by webhook or polling.
messages.wire: JSON-RPC result over MCP; long-running A2A tasks report over SSE (message/stream) or webhook push notifications.

messages.label: typed result or typed error
messages.carries: A typed result or a typed error — never an exception the loop has to interpret from prose.
messages.story: A typed result: success, with the new address identifier. Never an exception the loop has to interpret from prose.
messages.contract: Declared error semantics, so failure is a value the planner can reason about.
watch: Errors flattened into strings, so the planner retries the wrong thing
messages.how: Result and error unions declared in the tool contract so failure is a value the planner can act on.
messages.wire: JSON-RPC result or typed JSON error over the same MCP session.

messages.label: observe, then re-plan
messages.carries: The outcome of the action, and whatever the system now knows that it did not before.
messages.story: The orchestrator observes success. The task is complete, so the loop ends after one pass.
messages.contract: Structured result appended to durable state, then re-planned against.
watch: Looping without progress because nothing measures whether the result advanced the task
Budget consumed by iterations that never converge
messages.how: Result appended to durable state; loop guard checks progress, step count and budget before another iteration.
stack: LangGraph state + checkpointer or Temporal history
messages.wire: In-process or gRPC return to the orchestrator; appended to Temporal event history / the checkpointer.

messages.label: write back what earns persistence
messages.carries: The facts, episodes or procedures this task earned the right to persist.
messages.story: Worth remembering: Maya prefers office delivery on weekdays. Retained twelve months, no card data, her tenant only.
messages.contract: Write policy decision, with TTL and redaction applied before storage.
watch: Persisting everything by default, which degrades recall and creates retention liability
messages.how: Write policy decides what persists; redact, set TTL and partition by tenant before storing.
messages.wire: REST to the memory service (Mem0/Zep) or gRPC to the vector store; TTL set on the record.

messages.label: validate the final output
messages.carries: The completed result, or the partial result plus the reason the loop stopped.
messages.story: The final answer is drafted. Validate it before it is said.
messages.contract: Final output with the termination reason attached.
watch: Partial results presented as complete because the stop reason was dropped
messages.how: Output rails: schema validation, policy classifiers and redaction before anything is emitted.
stack: Guardrails AI or NeMo output rails
messages.wire: Synchronous gRPC (mTLS) to the guardrail service; REST fallback.

messages.label: schema-valid and policy-clean
messages.carries: Output that has passed schema and policy validation and been redacted where required.
messages.story: Schema fine, no data Maya does not already have, policy clean.
messages.contract: Schema-valid, policy-clean payload, or a controlled failure path.
watch: Validation applied to the final message only, while intermediate steps already acted
Silent redaction that leaves the reader with a misleading answer
messages.how: Validation result attached to the response envelope as an attestation the gateway can check.
messages.wire: gRPC response carrying the validation attestation to the gateway.

messages.label: metered and charged to the tenant
messages.carries: The response, with the token cost of the whole task counted and charged to the tenant.
messages.story: Four thousand one hundred tokens metered and charged to the retail tenant — cost per successful task, not per call.
messages.contract: Cost record keyed to the same trace ID as the work it paid for.
watch: Cost aggregated per call rather than per successful task, hiding the real unit economics
messages.how: Token spend aggregated per task and tenant; infrastructure share joined for cost per successful task.
messages.wire: Internal HTTPS/JSON to the surface; spend record published asynchronously on Kafka for FinOps.

messages.label: answer, with provenance
messages.carries: The answer, streamed, with provenance and any refusals or uncertainties stated plainly.
messages.story: “Done — order #48213 will ship to your office. Here is what changed.” Streamed, with the evidence it was based on.
messages.contract: An answer plus the evidence needed to calibrate trust in it.
watch: Fluency mistaken for grounding because provenance was not shown
Refusals presented as errors, teaching users to route around the control
messages.how: Stream the answer with citations and explicit refusal or uncertainty states rendered in the interface.
messages.wire: SSE or WebSocket stream to the user (AG-UI events); HTTPS response for API callers.

messages.label: a span for every hop
messages.carries: A span for every hop in the sequence above, carrying trace, thread and task IDs, the acting identity, the policy decision and the cost. Drawn once here; emitted by every exchange in the diagram.
messages.story: Every hop above emitted a span carrying the same trace ID, the acting identity, the policy decision and the cost.
messages.contract: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions; correlation survives queues, handoffs and approval waits.
watch: Correlation broken at an asynchronous boundary, which makes replay impossible
Instrumentation retrofitted after launch — the most expensive omission in this whole composition
messages.how: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions on every hop, with trace, thread and task IDs propagated across queues and waits.
messages.wire: OTLP over gRPC (4317) — or HTTP/protobuf (4318) — from every service to the OpenTelemetry Collector.

messages.label: traces become eval cases
messages.carries: Production traces converted into evaluation cases, especially the ones that failed.
messages.story: This trace joins the evaluation set: an approval path with a human in it is exactly the kind of case worth keeping.
messages.contract: Every incident becomes a permanent regression case.
watch: Incidents closed without a test, so the same failure returns
messages.how: Trace-to-dataset pipeline that turns production traces, especially failures, into evaluation cases.
messages.wire: Batch: trace export to object storage or Kafka; eval service pulls over HTTPS REST.

messages.label: evidence for the release gate
messages.carries: Evidence a release gate can act on: pass rates by scope, variance across runs, attack success rate, cost per successful task.
messages.story: Next week’s release is gated on this case still passing, across repeated runs.
messages.contract: Scores published with the harness and judge configuration that produced them.
watch: A single passing run treated as proof
Judges never calibrated against human graders
messages.how: Evaluation in CI: repeated runs, adversarial suites, scores published with the judge configuration.
stack: Inspect AI or promptfoo in CI
messages.wire: CI webhook (HTTPS) and a REST call to the release gate; results as JSON artefacts.

messages.label: redeploy versioned artefacts
messages.carries: Approved changes — versioned agents, prompts, models, tools and policies — deployed by canary or shadow with rollback ready.
messages.story: The approved prompt and tool versions redeploy by canary.
messages.contract: Registry-tracked change with an owner and a way back.
watch: Changes applied straight to production because the canary path was never built
Shadow agents outside any registry, so changes cannot be governed at all
messages.how: Prompts, models, tools and policies versioned in a registry and released by canary with rollback.
messages.wire: GitOps: Argo Rollouts CRDs via the Kubernetes API (HTTPS); model/prompt versions from the registry’s REST API (MLflow).

messages.label: policy compiled into enforcement
messages.carries: Policy authored in governance, compiled into the rules guardrails actually enforce at runtime.
messages.story: A policy refinement — address changes on paid orders always require approval — is compiled into the guardrails.
messages.contract: Policy-as-code, versioned and deployed like any other artefact.
watch: Written standard and deployed rules drifting apart, which makes the policy decorative
messages.how: Policy authored in git, tested, and shipped as a versioned bundle to the enforcement points.
stack: OPA bundles or Cedar policy store
messages.wire: OPA bundle download over HTTPS (bundle polling) or Cedar policy store REST; policy tested in CI first.

messages.label: capacity, cost and availability
messages.carries: Platform capacity, cost and availability, so infrastructure economics sit in the same picture as token economics.
messages.story: Infrastructure reports the sandbox cost and GPU utilisation into the same picture as the token spend.
messages.contract: Cost and utilisation records joined to the same tenant and trace dimensions.
watch: GPU cost and token cost reported separately, so nobody owns cost per successful task
messages.how: Platform metrics exported with tenant and trace dimensions so infrastructure cost sits beside token cost.
messages.wire: Prometheus remote-write (HTTP/protobuf) or OTLP metrics to the same collector; cost records over HTTPS.

ticks.note: Fan-out. Governed data and memory recall are independent, so retrieval asks both at once.
Fan-in. Retrieval waits for the slower of the two, then assembles.
Asynchronous. The task is checkpointed and waits for a human — seconds to days — holding no compute while it waits.
Branch not taken in this run. A reversible, low-impact action would have proceeded unattended, fully logged.
Sandbox provisioning and the address classifier are independent; both start immediately.
Loop decision. A partial result would send the loop back to step 6; several tools or peer agents would fan out from here in parallel.
Write-back is off the critical path: memory persists asynchronously while the answer is validated and delivered.
Continuous, not a step. Spans and platform metrics were emitted at every hop above — drawn once here so they can be seen.
Offline loop, hours to days later.

clarification.label: ask the user
clarification.carries: A clarifying question. The request was under-specified; asking is cheaper than guessing.
clarification.contract: Durable interrupt: the workflow checkpoints and waits for the answer, holding no compute.
clarification.how: Orchestrator raises a clarification interrupt; the surface renders the question with the options the planner needs.
clarification.wire: Durable interrupt over gRPC (Temporal) or the checkpointer; question pushed to the surface as AG-UI events over SSE.
watch: Asking for everything up front instead of the one thing that blocks the plan

clarification.label: clarifying question
clarification.carries: The question, in the channel the user is already in.
clarification.how: Streamed prompt with structured choices where possible.
clarification.wire: SSE or WebSocket to the user’s channel.
watch: Free-text questions where a choice would do

clarification.label: answer
clarification.carries: The answer, which is untrusted input like any other.
clarification.contract: Screened by the guardrails before it touches state.
clarification.how: Answer captured, screened, and attached to the session.
clarification.wire: HTTPS POST from the surface; screened before it touches state.
watch: Treating the answer as more trusted than the original request

clarification.label: clarified request
clarification.carries: The clarified request appended to durable state; planning resumes from the checkpoint.
clarification.contract: Resume from snapshot with the answer in state.
clarification.how: Workflow resumed with the answer; the plan is regenerated, not patched.
clarification.wire: Temporal Signal over gRPC resumes the workflow; state appended.
watch: Resuming without re-planning, so the original wrong assumption survives

trigger.label: signal arrives
trigger.carries: A trigger, not a request: a forecast, a monitor, a schedule or an upstream event the agent is subscribed to.
trigger.contract: Event on a governed channel with a source identity; the agent decides whether it warrants a task at all.
trigger.how: Event subscription into the channel adapter; deduplicate and rate-limit triggers; open a task with the source recorded as the actor.
trigger.wire: Event subscription: Kafka or NATS wire protocol over TCP (mTLS); MQTT for sensor-originated triggers; HTTPS webhook for SaaS feeds. Deduplicated by event id.
watch: A trigger that opens a task for every event, flooding humans with proposals
No source identity on the event, so a forged alert looks like a real one

dialogue.label: agent proposes
dialogue.carries: The agent’s suggestion, with the evidence, the action it wants to take and an explicit ask for confirmation.
dialogue.contract: Proposal shown in the human’s channel; nothing executes until they answer.
dialogue.how: Proposal card with evidence, options and confirm / amend controls; a durable wait behind it.
dialogue.wire: Proposal card as AG-UI events over SSE/WebSocket to the human’s channel; the workflow waits on a durable interrupt (gRPC / checkpointer).
watch: A proposal without the evidence, so the human rubber-stamps

dialogue.label: human replies
dialogue.carries: A question, an amendment or a decision — untrusted input, screened like the trigger was.
dialogue.contract: Screened, attached to the session, appended to durable state.
dialogue.how: Reply captured as a structured choice or free text; guardrails screen it; state updated.
dialogue.wire: HTTPS POST from the surface; screened by the guardrail service (gRPC) before it reaches state.
watch: Treating the reply as more trusted because it came from an approver

dialogue.label: agent answers
dialogue.carries: The answer to the human’s question, from the context the agent already holds.
dialogue.contract: Answered from state; no new side effects while the human is deciding.
dialogue.how: Answer from the assembled context; a new tool call only if the question genuinely needs one.
dialogue.wire: SSE/WebSocket to the human’s channel, answered from state.
watch: Re-planning silently while the human thinks they are still deciding

dialogue.label: human confirms
dialogue.carries: The confirmation or amendment, which becomes the approver’s recorded input at the gate.
dialogue.contract: Decision written to the audit trail with the approver identity before anything resumes.
dialogue.how: Decision captured, attributed, and signalled to the waiting workflow.
dialogue.wire: HTTPS POST from the surface; Temporal Signal over gRPC resumes the workflow; audit record appended over HTTPS.
watch: A confirmation that resumes the workflow without recording who gave it

intent.label: classify intent, draft the plan
intent.carries: The raw request, in the user’s words. Before anything is retrieved, a model has to decide what is being asked and which journey this is.
intent.contract: Routed through the gateway to a small model tier or a fine-tuned intent classifier; the frontier model is not needed for this.
intent.how: Intent classification and plan drafting on a small instruction-tuned model (or a classical classifier for a closed intent set), returning a structured intent with confidence and a plan skeleton.
stack: small model tier via LiteLLM routing
fine-tuned intent classifier (setfit / fastText) for closed sets
intent.wire: HTTPS REST (OpenAI-compatible JSON) through the gateway to the small-model tier — or gRPC to an intent-classifier service; W3C traceparent header.
watch: Low-confidence intents executed instead of clarified
Using the frontier model for every intent call, which is where most of the cost of a simple journey goes

intent.label: intent and plan, structured
intent.carries: A structured intent with a confidence score, and a plan skeleton the orchestrator executes deterministically when no further judgement is needed.
intent.contract: Schema-valid intent object; below the confidence threshold the plan is a clarification, not an action.
intent.how: Intent object validated at the boundary; confidence threshold from the intent’s risk class; the plan skeleton selects the journey template.
intent.wire: HTTPS REST response; intent object validated against JSON Schema.
watch: A plan skeleton that hard-codes tool calls the intent did not justify

secondPass.6: Second pass: the planner re-reads the task with the new state.
secondPass.7: Second pass: definitions unchanged; the ground truth still holds.
secondPass.8: Second pass: gather only what changed.
secondPass.9: Second pass: re-query the rows the outcome may have altered.
secondPass.10: Second pass: fresh rows, lineage appended.
secondPass.11: Second pass: anything new to recall?
secondPass.12: Second pass: nothing new; the earlier recall stands.
secondPass.13: Second pass: the context is rebuilt around the updated state, still inside budget.
secondPass.14: Second pass: reason again over the updated state.
secondPass.15: Second pass: routed and metered like the first; the prefix is still cached.
secondPass.16: The model reads the updated context.
secondPass.18: Second pass: a revised, schema-valid action.
secondPass.19: Second pass: is the revised action allowed to run unattended?
secondPass.20: Second pass: this action does not need a human.
secondPass.21: Second pass: no human decision required.
secondPass.22: Second pass: the revised action is reversible and low impact, so it proceeds unattended, fully logged.
secondPass.23: Second pass: execute the revised call with a new idempotency key.
secondPass.24: Second pass: the sandbox from the first pass is reused.
secondPass.25: Second pass: the sandbox is still warm.
secondPass.26: Second pass: the classifier is asked again with the new inputs.
secondPass.28: Second pass: same contract, same boundary.
secondPass.29: Second pass: the revised call goes out.
secondPass.30: Second pass: the result comes back.
secondPass.32: The orchestrator observes success. The task is complete after two passes.
